pr2_laundry_shift.text: Your shift is the laundry. Forty orange jumpsuits, one broken dryer, and a guard who counts the bleach like it's gold.

choices.wash_contraband: Hide a package in the wash

outcomes.paid: Someone pays you in cigarettes and respect. Both are currency.
outcomes.caught: A guard finds it. You find the hole.

pr2_kitchen_shift.text: Kitchen duty. Tonight's menu is a grey stew nobody can name. You are, technically, the chef.

outcomes.feast: Your block eats like kings for one night. You are briefly beloved.
outcomes.busted: The head cook catches you and your ribs meet his ladle.

pr2_library_shift.text: You shelve books in the prison library. The true crime section is very popular, which feels like a conflict of interest.

pr2_gang_initiation.text: Three men corner you in the shower block. The tall one says the Crows could use a face like yours. It is not a compliment.

outcomes.respect: They shrug. Respect, or maybe just scheduling.
outcomes.beaten: They explain the offer again, slower, with fists.

pr2_gang_war.text: Word comes down: the Crows are at war with the block next door. Tonight, in the yard, you are expected to be useful.

outcomes.won: You win the yard. Your knuckles lose.
outcomes.hurt: A pipe finds your shoulder. The infirmary finds you.
outcomes.hole: Guards flood the yard. You get thirty days alone with your thoughts.
outcomes.dead: A blade you never saw finds you between the ribs.

pr2_gang_tax.text: The Crows collect dues every month. Your share is whatever is in your commissary account, give or take your dignity.

outcomes.ok: They let it slide. This time.
outcomes.lesson: They teach a short lesson in arithmetic.

pr2_gang_leave.text: You're tired of the Crows. Leaving is possible, they say. The usual method involves a stretcher.

outcomes.free: A nod. A debt. You're out, mostly.
outcomes.beat_out: They beat you out the door, an exit interview of sorts.

pr2_cellmate_confession.text: At 3 a.m. your cellmate confesses something that makes your own sentence look like a parking ticket.

pr2_contraband_phone.text: A phone appears under your pillow, charged, with one bar of signal. Somebody wants a favour in return.

choices.sell: Rent it out by the minute

outcomes.sweet: Four minutes of a familiar voice. Better than any meal.
outcomes.shakedown: Raid at dawn. They find it, and they find you.

pr2_corrupt_guard.text: Officer Dunmore leans on your cell door. For two hundred dollars a month he can find you better food, a quieter block, and amnesia.

outcomes.cleaned: An investigation, a transfer, a cake. Someone cares, briefly.
outcomes.retaliation: Your cell gets searched daily. Your mattress develops opinions.

pr2_visit_no_show_spouse.text: Visiting day. You wait in the clean shirt. {{name}} doesn't come. No call, no note.

pr2_visit_no_show_child.text: Your kid was supposed to visit. The guard shrugs: nobody on the list today. {{name}} is probably busy. Probably.

pr2_class_education.text: The prison offers a class: Intro to Something. The teacher is a retired accountant who has never been so listened to.

choices.top_student: Aim for top of the class

outcomes.star: A certificate with your name. Your first in years.
outcomes.mocked: Cellmates call you Professor. It is not affectionate.

pr2_appeal_letter.text: You draft an appeal. A lawyer you can't afford says there is a thin chance to shave time. Thin, but chances usually are.

outcomes.granted: A year knocked off. The judge sneezes, you sign.
outcomes.denied: Denied, in two paragraphs and a stamp.

pr2_hunger_strike.text: The block is starting a hunger strike over the food. You're asked to join. Your stomach has opinions.

outcomes.win: Menu improved to 'edible'. A victory of sorts.
outcomes.lose: Nothing changes. You are thinner and still in prison.

pr2_transfer.text: At dawn they wake you: pack up, you're transferred. Nobody says where. The bus has no windows.

outcomes.stay: A clerk error saves you. Bureaucracy, ally.
outcomes.worse: You go anyway, and your new block has no heating.

pr2_tattoo.text: A man named Gus runs a tattoo operation with a staple, ink from a pen, and a steadier hand than a surgeon.

outcomes.good: Not bad. Slightly crooked. Entirely yours.
outcomes.infected: The skin gets angry. So does the infirmary nurse.

pr2_snitch_dilemma.text: You overheard who stabbed the kid in D-block. The warden offers you a better cell for a name. The yard offers a longer life for silence.

outcomes.safe: They move you quietly. The warden remembers.
outcomes.marked: Someone calls you a rat in a very loud voice. Then a fist.

pr2_talent_show.text: The chaplain organises a prison talent show. Prize: a pizza. Competition: fierce, and mostly beatboxing.

outcomes.standing: The hall goes wild. Even the guards clap, then deny it.
outcomes.flop: Silence. Then a cough. Then someone throws a sock.

pr2_parole_board.text: Parole board day. Five tired faces, a folder with your whole life in it, and ten minutes to prove you're changed.

outcomes.granted: Granted. They stamp it and you finally exhale.
outcomes.denied: Denied. Reapply in a year, they say, as though it's a library card.
outcomes.granted2: It cost a fortune. Worth it.

pr2_last_meal.text: The warden asks what you want for your last meal. They've been asking a while. You haven't picked yet.

pr2_final_appeal.text: Your lawyer arrives with a clemency file the size of a phone book. One last appeal before the date is set.

outcomes.commuted: Life, not death. The word 'life' has never sounded so good.
outcomes.executed: The court declines. They set a morning.
outcomes.stay: A stay, nothing more. You wait.

pr2_pen_pal.text: A stranger writes to you from another state. She says she writes to people on death row for fun. You have never felt so seen, awkwardly.

outcomes.bond: A friendship by post. The mailman is jealous.
outcomes.story: She sells your letters to a magazine.

pr2_chaplain_visit.text: The chaplain visits twice a week now. He has brought tea and no answers.

pr2_probation_checkin.text: A random check-in. Your officer, Pruitt, turns up unannounced, counts your empty bottles and your full fridge, and nods.

outcomes.clean: He misses it. You sweat through two shirts.
outcomes.caught: He finds it. Your probation becomes an extension.

pr2_probation_temptation.text: An old friend calls with a job that pays in cash and silence. You are on probation. The money is very good.

outcomes.rich: Nobody notices. You buy a coat.
outcomes.violated: Violation. The cell remembers your shape.

pr2_probation_job.text: Interviews are bleak. Every employer ticks the same box, then your résumé disappears. One diner doesn't tick it.

pr2_commissary.text: Commissary day: soup packets, instant coffee, toothpaste. In here, a stamp is a salary and a candy bar is a vow.

pr2_yard_chess.text: An old lifer challenges you to chess. Rumour says he hasn't lost in 22 years.

outcomes.win: You win. He buys you tea and a new respect.
outcomes.lose: You lose in nine moves and learn a great deal.

pr2_lockdown.text: Lockdown. Somebody smuggled in something, and the whole wing pays for it with 72 hours in the cell and cold sandwiches.

pr2_new_fish.text: A trembling new inmate gets the bunk above yours. He's about nineteen and entirely too clean.

outcomes.ok: He cries a little. You keep the socks.
outcomes.retaliate: It turns out he has a big brother in the block.

pr2_ex_letter.text: A letter from {{name}}. Your ex wants to know whether you've thought about them. Also, they need to send your boxes back.

pr2_mother_letter.text: A letter from {{name}}. Your mother's handwriting, with lists of what she has cooked for you and has no way to send.

pr2_probation_curfew.text: Your curfew is 9 p.m. A friend just invited you to the one party that mentions no names and no police.

outcomes.fun: The best night in years. Nobody checks.
outcomes.check: The officer rings your landline. You are not near it.

pr2_hooch.text: Somebody is brewing hooch from fruit cups and bread in a trash bag. It smells like regret in a bottle.

outcomes.sick: Your head files a complaint that lasts a week.

pr2_guard_beating.text: A guard decides you looked at him wrong. His colleague looks away with the practised ease of a man who has done so before.

outcomes.lucky: The camera happens to be working. He gets suspended.
outcomes.worse: You go to the hole, he goes to lunch.

pr2_interview.text: A podcaster wants your story. She's earnest, underpaid, and only a little exploitative.

outcomes.sympathy: Listeners write letters. Some even like you.

pr2_old_timer.text: A lifer shares a rule, free of charge: 'Don't owe anyone. Don't be anyone's favour. Don't be the loudest man in the yard.'

pr2_shakedown.text: Cell search. They toss your mattress, your books and your single photograph. One officer reads your letters aloud in funny voices.

outcomes.ignored: Nobody cares. Your letters are now crumpled.
outcomes.punished: Objection noted. Along with a cell with no light.

pr2_mess_riot.text: A fight in the mess hall becomes a riot. A tray flies over your head like a frisbee with ambitions.

outcomes.survive: You live. Your tray does not.
outcomes.hurt: A broken orbital and a story that's bad even by prison standards.
